The noodles were firm and chewy, so they had a nice chewy texture, and they went well with the soup, so it was delicious to eat without getting tired of it. Even though it wasn't spicy, the flavor was still there, so it was easy to enjoy without pressure, and I was even more satisfied because it felt warm and refreshing at the same time. Beef and shrimp tempura kake udon is different from the mosi clam udon soup.
Perhaps because the broth was boiled every day, it felt really rich.
The udon noodles are really chewy and springy, perhaps because they are kneaded by blending flour for more than 4 hours and aged at high and low temperatures, so they are very soft and delicious.
The fried shrimp was also really great, with plump shrimp meat.
I ordered 2 pieces and then ordered 2 more pieces👍👍

My girlfriend and I ordered negi, seasonal sashimi for two, Moriawase, futomaki, and green tangerine highball for two.
The signature Negi green onion dish is made with charcoal-flavored green onions mixed with basil miso cream, so you can't stop eating it on a baguette.

The sashimi was beautifully plated and each part was aged differently, so not a single piece was boring.

The green tangerine highball is refreshing and slightly bitter at the end, making it a good pairing with a clover. After eating the futomaki, there was enough food for two people to fill our stomachs.

reviews.text: Sponsored // If you are looking for an izakaya in Garosu-gil with a good atmosphere and satisfying food, I felt that Negi Dining Lounge is a place worth considering. As soon as I entered the store, I was impressed by the open kitchen structure and calm lounge atmosphere. I had high expectations because it was run by a chef who appeared on Black and White Chef, but I was actually very satisfied with the quality of each dish. In particular, the seasonal sashimi moriawase was fresh from the looks of it, and each fish had a different texture and flavor, so it was fun to eat, and it was clean without any unpleasant smell, so it was a great first menu item. The signature dish, Negi, was impressive because the green onion flesh with a subtle charcoal scent was so soft and sweet, and the combination with the basil miso cream sauce was so harmonious that I never got tired of it. Shrimp Lotus Root Hasami-age was crispy on the outside and plump on the inside, providing a great contrast in texture. When eaten with the shoe cream sauce, the flavor came to life and went well with drinks. Hakushu DR Highball had a refreshing and smoky flavor, so it was good to go with food, and it felt like it organized the flow of the entire meal. The staff's response was calm and attentive, so I was able to eat comfortably. Overall, I got the impression that it was a Garosu-gil izakaya with a good balance of food, atmosphere, and service, so I was willing to visit again.

The tteokbokki I ate at Bad Penguin near Gangnam Station was spicy, so as I was thinking about a menu to counteract the spiciness, I remembered the Apgujeong branch near my house among the Katsuo chain restaurants that I had not been to yet, so I decided to stop by.

I knew the location of the store while passing by before, so I found it easily. When I entered the store, it wasn't as big as the previous Yeoksam branch, but about the size of the Dogok branch, the main branch of Katsuo. There were a lot of customers, so I wondered if there would be a seat, but fortunately, there was an empty table for two, so I checked the QR code and sat down. They brought me a pitcher of water and a menu, and said that menchi katsu was not possible, but I asked for the loin cutlet set meal, which I always order.

When I first visited the Yeoksam branch, it was surprisingly good, so I wondered if the main branch would be better, so I inquired which branch was the main branch. The nuance of the reply that the Dogok branch felt like the main branch made me feel like each branch was run independently. When I also visited the Dogok branch, which is called the main branch, I thought that was because the brand was the same but the food was slightly different. I was curious how the Apgujeong branch would be different.

After waiting for some time due to the backlog of orders, the loin cutlet set meal I ordered was finally brought out on a tray. The visual appearance of the loin cutlet was similar to that of the Dogok branch, which was slightly thicker but slightly less tasty than the Yeoksam branch, which had the best taste but was a bit thinner.

First, when I tasted the miso soup, it was just salty, and the cabbage salad was sprinkled with a common sesame dressing, but it felt sweet, so it was a bit far from the type I liked.

The loin cutlet is not as thick as the premium tonkatsu shops, but I thought it would be thick and slightly pink, so I asked for salt. As it wasn't a premium tonkatsu shop like other katsuo restaurants, the kitchen brought seasoned salt to me. I leaned in, sprinkled the seasoned salt on it, and tasted it. It was yummy.

It has a nice firm texture and a bit of resistance rather than being juicy, and it feels a bit stiff and has almost no juice, so I drink water and am quickly disappointed because I can feel the meaty flavor, which is not bad, but not good.

That's why I eat it with mustard rather than salt and dip it in the sweet tonkatsu sauce, and since it doesn't feel delicious, I feel like I want to eat it quickly and leave rather than enjoy it slowly and savor it.

Overall, Katsuou's Loin Cutlet, which I stopped at near Katsuou Yeoksam branch, was better than I expected, so I stopped by Dogok branch, and I also stopped by Apgujeong branch near my house, which was the last store. It was the worst experience among them, but it was okay because I didn't think I could eat it.

reviews.author: Dominic Kim
reviews.text:
​After much deliberation, I made a reservation at Gold Tuna Sinsa branch as it coincided with an important business meeting and anniversary. To sum up, I was so shocked that I thought the tuna I had been eating was fake. From the clean interior that blends in with the sophisticated atmosphere near Sinsa Station to the polite hospitality felt at the entrance, even before eating, I was confident that I had come to the right place today.
​The biggest feature here is the fully aged tuna. Usually, when I go to a tuna restaurant, I tend to wrap it in seaweed and eat it because it is not thawed enough, so it has a crunchy texture or the fishy smell of the water, but gold tuna is on a different level. As soon as I took my first bite, I realized why the manager confidently said, “Never eat our tuna wrapped in seaweed.” The moment it touches the tip of your tongue, the richness of the fat that melts away and the umami that has been condensed through the aging process explode, and the quality of the raw meat itself is so overwhelming that even a little wasabi and radish sprouts are enough.
​In particular, the marbling of Odoro and Judoro was like seeing the highest quality Korean beef, and thanks to the professional service that explained step by step how to eat each part in the most delicious way, I felt like I was receiving omakase-level treatment. The natural flavor of the tuna was maximized by dipping the oily parts in salt and lightly dipping the light parts in special soy sauce.
​The course dishes other than the main tuna are also excellent. From the mouth-watering tuna porridge and salad, to the classic tofu steak on the outside, and the savory grilled tuna without any fishy smell, there was nothing to be wasted. The fried food served in the middle was crispy, as expected from a Japanese restaurant, and the jiri soup served at the end had a deep, refreshing soup flavor that made me feel like I was instantly cured from the alcohol I had been drinking.
​You may think the price is a bit high, but considering the level of parts provided and the quality of service, it feels like good value for money. There is also a private space where you can focus on conversation, so I would highly recommend it as a place to bring a special person or celebrate an anniversary with your lover.
​On the way out, I exchanged greetings with the manager and said, “I’ll be back again soon,” not as empty words, but with sincerity. If you want to enjoy authentic tuna in Sinsa-dong, don’t hesitate and go to Gold Tuna Sinsa Branch. I immediately saved it to my list of restaurants in my life.

Yasunoyajiro, a lamb specialty restaurant located in Apgujeong

First of all, the store is not that large and all seats are counter seats. The atmosphere feels like you're in Japan.

I ordered the Oosme set (3.5 pieces), which is said to be the most expensive, and all parts of lamb were delicious with almost no unpleasant odor.
It was convenient because the staff took charge of grilling the meat.
And the raw lamb hamburger was really delicious. Hamburg made from lamb is cooked with a torch, and it is surprisingly delicious. If you have some hamburger leftover, you can cook it with rice, and at the end, you can enjoy ochasuke.

This place has a nice feel, the food is delicious, and the price is reasonable.

Even though they are the same cut, the Jingisukan was very soft and savory with just the right amount of fat, while the Katamari had a firm texture. The green onions that were grilled together were very sweet and tasty, so I asked for more, and they grilled more than enough. The popular lamb hamburger is served medium-rare, and while the previous raw meat had no foul odor at all, the hamburger had a unique lamb flavor, so I personally wasn't as impressed with it as the raw meat, and I didn't feel that the rice that was said to use Koshihikari was particularly good.

The taste of Sapporo draft beer was very good. It had a smooth texture and taste just like what you get in Japan, and it went very well with the fatty lamb.

You can enjoy a delicious meal with table vinegar or Japanese oil. Adding a little vinegar closes the flavor profile and doesn't stop the chopsticks even in the second half. Rayu is a fragrant type that adds umami rather than spiciness.

The ingredients include juicy pork shoulder loin, menma with just the right amount of fiber, and fragrant green onions. They are all well-balanced with fabrics that make the noodles stand out.

I was surprised that you can eat authentic oil side dishes all the way from Seoul to here. The quality is comparable to that of Japanese specialty stores. The aftertaste was light and easy to eat, and although it was crowded at peak times, the serving was relatively smooth.

Tuna smoked in rice bran will likely be remembered for quite a long time. Personally, I don't like cooked tuna, but Rayho's tuna is excellent. Also, in a similar way, tilefish, geumtae, cutlassfish, and anago are grilled using charcoal and rice straw, which maximizes the natural taste of the ingredients and makes the oil flow well.

If you look at the reviews before visiting, many people said that it tastes like mainland Japan, but after trying the sushi, I think I understand. Neta is mostly aged quite a bit and has a soft texture, while shari has a strong sour taste and has a sea flavor unique to aged sushi. Personally, I feel similar to Sushi Koji. The overall harmony was better with white fish than with hikarimono, and in particular, the madai was delicious enough to be requested as an encore as the chive scent, texture, and shari went well together. The benjari, which was served with the skin charcoal-fried, was also delicious. Uniquely, chawanmushi is served in the middle of the sushi. It is topped with pea sauce, and has a pudding-like texture and fragrant taste, making it the best I've ever had at Sushiya.

However, the disappointing part is that most neta has a similar texture and shari is a bit sour, so it feels like there is a lack of variety even though there are many types of sushi. (The taste is almost the same... Of course, tsumami using rice straw and charcoal is very good.)

I look forward to the day when I can visit again.

There were celebrity autographs all over the walls, so I thought this restaurant was more famous than I thought. They also had a course menu, so I'm planning to go there next time for a company dinner.

reviews.author: Kai Lee
reviews.text:
Sinsa Station Chinese Restaurant Cheonmimi
Clean and delicious Chinese restaurant. It's not difficult to make a reservation, it's close to the station, there are a lot of rooms, and there's a corkage-free policy for orders over a certain amount per person, so it's great for gatherings.
Lunch Miset 5 items of cold vegetables - crab meat soup - Jeongabok - Eohyangdongo - Red pepper japchae - Meal (Choose one of Jjajang, Jjamppong, fried rice + egg soup) All suited my taste.

reviews.author: YJ YANG
reviews.text:
A place with high ceilings and well-appointed rooms!
For the food, I ordered Eohyangdonggo, Kkuvarou, Menbosha, cream shrimp, grilled dumplings, and tray jjajang, and all of them were delicious except for the cream shrimp, which had a very thick batter.

reviews.author: Kiyoung's older brother, Kicheol
reviews.text: The store is spacious and clean. The staff were also friendly. The visual of whole squid chadol jjamppong is the best.

reviews.author: D.W.C Love
reviews.text: This is a place I always stop by for lunch once a week. It is the most delicious and cost-effective among all the Chinese restaurants in the neighborhood. There are daily menus and mixed menus. Personally, I think the red pepper tray jjajang is the most delicious.

reviews.author: Park Yun-cheol
reviews.text:
An old, long-established Chinese restaurant in Sinsa-dong
It's been a while since I went to Jeongnam, but the prices have risen a lot.
I ate sweet and sour pork with black bean paste set.
Still, I ate a lot of Jjamppong soup.

reviews.author: Kwon Y.J
reviews.text:
Red pepper tray jjajang!!!!!! I have a younger brother who goes to work 3-4 times a week just to eat this haha. My office location is a bit far away so I can't go often, but this is the best Chinese food in Shinsa!! Tangshyuk is also delicious~ Jjamppong is a basic Jjamppong, but the soup is subtly refreshing and not too spicy, which is good~
Be sure to try the red pepper tray jjajang.

reviews.author: J Lee
reviews.text: There aren't many places in Sinsa-dong where you can get a meal at this price. Considering the price, the portion is generous and tasty. In particular, the sweet and sour pork is an old-fashioned Cantonese style sweet and sour pork, so it is crunchy and has a nice sour taste.

reviews.author: I like the mountains behind

The taste isn't bad, but I think they captured the concept of uni well.
The eggplant rice bowl was so delicious that I saved it for Baemin delivery.
I felt the balance was good because the onions were cooked well and added well.

You must try uni dumplings!! With water dumplings!

The staff was nice and friendly too.

reviews.author: Minji
reviews.text: It's not the dumplings I always eat, but there are dumplings on the new menu. The uni and mackerel dumplings are unique and the taste is new, so it's good to go at least once. I get sick of eating only dumplings, so it's good to eat them with soupy dishes as well.

reviews.author: Takbo-seong

I ordered dumplings, noodles, rice, and even appetizers, and they were all delicious.
The soup for steamed dumplings is hot, so pour the soup with a spoon like you would dim sum.
Grilled mackerel dumplings go well with mackerel dumplings.

reviews.author: technology of leisure
reviews.text:
There are signs saying that famous celebrities visited and ate there.
Orders are placed at a small kiosk at the table, and it is made of transparent glass so you can see the food being cooked.
Once you order, the food comes out quickly and the taste is good.
Instead, if you compare it to an adult male, the amount may be a little small.
The store is not large, and is a space where about 20 customers can sit and eat.
The food tastes good so I recommend it.
I think it's worth eating at least once.
